title: Desk Guidance Note — Inpatient Stays, Suspension and Breaks in Need on PAP Therapy Equipment
content:
# Inpatient Stays, Suspension and Breaks in Need — PAP Therapy Equipment

**Suspension.** When the patient is admitted to a hospital or skilled nursing facility, the PAP Therapy Equipment device record is suspended with the admission date as the suspended date; rental is not billed for any month whose first day falls during the suspension.

**Resumption in the same period.** When the patient is home again the rental resumes in the same rental period, with the paid months counted so far carried forward. A suspended rental resumes only when the patient comes home no later than the class's break-in-need days after the suspension began, counting calendar days from the day after the suspended date, the allowance being the class's break-in-need days plus the days remaining in the rental month in which the suspension began.

**A longer break.** A longer break ends the rental period: the record resumes with a new rental period whose rental period start date is the return-home date and whose month count starts again at 1, and billing waits for the class's requirements for a new rental period.

**Planned absences.** A suspension is never used for a planned absence such as travel; the device stays rented and billed.

## The time gate, element by element

| Element | Rule |
|---|---|
| Event the clock starts from | the suspension beginning, as the suspended date on the device record shows |
| First day counted | the day after the suspended date |
| Unit | calendar days |
| Allowance | the class's break-in-need days plus the days remaining in the rental month in which the suspension began |
| Comparison | the return home is no later than the last day of the allowance; that last day itself is within it |
| Within the allowance | resumes in the same rental period, paid months carried forward |
| Beyond the allowance | new rental period from the return-home date, month count from 1, billing waits for the class's new-period requirements |

## Boundary cases

- The patient comes home on the last day of the allowance: the rental resumes in the same rental period.
- The patient comes home on the day after the last day of the allowance: the rental period ends and a new one starts on the return-home date.
- The patient leaves for a two-week holiday: no suspension; the month continues to be billed.

**Allowance figure (hypothetical).** On a class with a 60-day break in need, a suspension that began with 9 days remaining in its rental month has an allowance of 60 plus 9, or 69 calendar days counted from the day after the suspended date.
